THE KEY FINDING IS NEGATIVE: THE STORY HAS NOT MOVED TODAY.
This BBC article is the source of the "until Sunday" deadline. It has not been updated since 18:37 BST on Friday — datePublished and dateModified are identical. As of 18:00 GMT on Sunday 25 October:
 - No Green group has been reported as responding on the record today.
 - Labour has said nothing new on the record today.
 - Labour's NEC has not met or decided.
 - A firecrawl news sweep for a Green/Labour/NEC development dated today returns only syndicated copies of this same Friday BBC article.
 - The BBC politics index carries no newer item on it.
 - gov.uk is irrelevant here (internal party matter) and in any case has published nothing since 24 October.
A deadline passing without a reported response is a legitimate thing to say, but it must be said as that and not as "no group responded" — absence of reporting is not absence of response.

WHAT THE FRIDAY ARTICLE ACTUALLY ESTABLISHES
"The BBC has been told Green groups have been given until Sunday to respond to the demand, after which Labour's ruling National Executive Committee (NEC) will decide whether the party will continue with local deals to share power." Note "the BBC has been told" — the deadline itself is unattributed.
"Green groups in some areas have publicly stated they do not agree with the policy or have distanced themselves from it, reducing the likelihood the pacts will end."
Nine local authorities where Greens are key power-sharing partners: Sheffield City Council, Warwick District Council and Lewes District Council (direct Labour-Green coalitions), plus West Oxfordshire District, Stafford Borough, Havant Borough, Broadland District, Derbyshire Dales District and Wealden District.
Already distanced from the policy: Lewes, Wealden, Broadland, West Sussex, North Somerset.
Runnymede Borough Council: Green councillors have left the local ruling alliance following Labour's ultimatum.
Stafford: the Greens hold one cabinet post, Cllr Tony Pearce (climate change portfolio). Labour confirmed that if the Greens refuse to reject the policy, a process would be triggered to remove Pearce from his cabinet position. Doug Rouxel, leader of the Stafford Green group, told the BBC they were "formulating a response" to Labour's letter which they would like to put to party members first. Pearce has not responded to a request for comment.
Lewes: Chris Collier, leader of the Labour group on the Green-led council, has RESIGNED FROM LABOUR over the tone of his own party's ultimatum and will sit as an independent cabinet member. He has been contacted for comment.
Rules asymmetry: Labour councillors need NEC approval to enter local tie-ups and the rulebook says local groups must "stand down" from power-sharing when asked by their regional office; the Green Party of England and Wales leaves the decision to local groups.
A Green Party spokesperson: "For the Labour government to conflate criticism of Israel with antisemitism is disappointing and wrong." / "Trying to tell local parties what to do and who they can work with is undemocratic."
Background: the "Zionism is racism" motion passed at the Green conference in Brighton last month; it described Zionism as an ideology supporting an "ethnonationalist Jewish state" that had led to the "disenfranchisement and destruction" of Palestinians, and backed "a single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine". Four of the Greens' five MPs have criticised it. Green leader Zack Polanski, who skipped the conference vote while campaigning in a Westminster by-election, has said he wants the "imperfect" motion amended in future.
